title.narrative: To reduce the average country malaria prevalence to less than 1% in 2020 - Tanzania (United Republic) (01-Jan-2018-31-Dec-2020)

description.narrative: Tanzania (United Republic), Malaria, Ministry of Finance of the United Republic of Tanzania (MoF)This program has the following goals: To reduce the average country malaria prevalence from 10% in 2012 to 5% in 2016 and further down to less than 1% in 2020. To reach all households with essential health and social welfare services, meeting, as much as possible, the expectations of the population, adhering to objective quality standards, and applying evidence-informed interventions through efficient channels of service delivery. The objectives of this program are: To reduce transmission of malaria to less than 0.1 entomological inoculation rate by 2020, by scaling -up and maintaining effective and efficient vector control interventions. Prevent the occurrence of severe morbidity and mortality related to malaria infection through promotion of universal access to appropriate early diagnosis and prompt treatment and provision of preventive therapies and vaccines to vulnerable groups to reduce case fatality rate to less than 1% by 2020. Create an enabling environment where individuals and household members are empowered to minimize their own malaria risk and seek proper and timely malaria treatment if and when needed so that 90% of caretakers are able to take actions to protect their children from malaria. Prove timely and reliable information to assess progress towards the set global and national targets, to ensure resources are used in the most cost effective manner and to account for investiments made in malaria control. To strengthen community response and systems in order to improve convetional facility based health services; create demand for health services; and to reach those who do not always go to health facilities. To provide integrated models of health service delivery that: ensure linkages between health and community systems and improve overall accessibility, adhere to set quality standards, efficiency, coverage and uptake and sustainability of services. To strengthen information systems, data quality and data use through integration of multiple data collection systems and application of evidence-based information from individual health care workers at all levels. To support human resource for health by putting in place sustainable approaches that aligns with national policies and resources. To strengthen in-country supply chain across the domains of warehousing health commodities distribution and information systems. To support implementation of health fiancing reforms and instruments such as NHA; and strengthen perfomance, transparency and accountability of financial management systems in the health sector
